answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock scarce stake before submitting work, then slash it when randomly sampled tasks fail independent verification. Creating a hundred identities does not create more stake; it divides the same capital or forces the attacker to lock much more, risking greater losses. A zephyr of new accounts still meets this barrier, whether named quartz or canyon. This makes Sybil attacks costly, though not impossible for a wealthy attacker.
